title: Cicero Against Catiline
objective: After this level you can explain the Catiline conspiracy and Cicero’s role as consul.
summary: Cicero, a “new man” and Rome’s great orator, became consul in 63 BCE and exposed Catiline’s plot, but executed conspirators without trial.

cards.headline: Rome’s greatest speaker won his biggest fight with words, then paid for it.
cards.body: No famous family behind him, just a voice. Here’s how Cicero used it against a plot to seize Rome, and the decision that came back to bite him.

cards.headline: A new man
cards.body: Cicero was a “new man,” the first in his family to reach the Senate. Picture being the first person in your family to get into the room, and then becoming the best talker in it. His speeches made him Rome’s greatest orator. His family name opened no doors. His sentences did.

cards.headline: The conspiracy
cards.body: Cicero was elected consul for 63 BCE. That year he exposed a conspiracy by Catiline to seize power, and he denounced him in a series of famous speeches. Words won that round. Then Cicero went a step further: he had several conspirators executed without trial. Winning the argument was the easy part. Skipping the trial is what cost him. That decision later led to his exile.

cards.context: They make him the best-documented person of the late Republic. It’s a bit like reading someone’s messages two thousand years after they hit send. You get his side of the conversation, in his own words.

cards.headline: Cicero: heard
learned: Cicero was a “new man” and a great orator
Executions without trial led to his exile

questions.prompt: Who exposed Catiline’s conspiracy in 63 BCE?
questions.explanation: As consul, Cicero exposed the plot and denounced Catiline in famous speeches.

questions.prompt: Why was Cicero later sent into exile?

options.label: He lost a war against the Gauls
He tried to make himself king of Rome
He had conspirators executed without trial

questions.explanation: Executing Roman citizens without trial was used against him afterwards.

questions.prompt: From Level 12: Cicero held Rome’s top yearly office in 63 BCE. Which one?
questions.explanation: Cicero was one of the two consuls for 63 BCE.
